solutions.check: 30 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Apparently an upper-class twit, George, involved with job scam

indicators.note: things involved are tangled up together, so the letters get mixed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A posh fool named George caught up in some employment fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: Jacob Rees-Mogg is the famously old-fashioned, plummy Conservative MP; 'Apparently' lets the setter off the hook for calling him a twit.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition is a satirical description of the politician, whose manner and accent caricature the aristocratic English toff.

clue.text: Panic! Foreign article found in member

indicators.note: to be found in something is to sit inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: an arm is a limb, a member of the body
la is the French and Spanish feminine definite article

explanation.surface: An exclamation of panic at discovering something foreign lodged in a body part.
explanation.walkthrough: The French word for 'the' sits between the first and second letters of the limb.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarm as a noun is sudden fear or fright, the same state of mind as panic.

clue.text: Conservative getting on fishy group

blocks.note: someone getting on is ageing
a school is a shoal of fish

explanation.surface: A Tory politician getting along with some suspicious-looking faction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conservative' wants to be the party, and 'fishy' wants to mean suspect; here it is lower-case traditional, and fishy is literally about fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Old-school describes someone attached to traditional ways and values, which is what conservative means in its general sense.

clue.text: Gents not elected after start of ruin of the country

indicators.note: saying something is not there tells you to take it away from the word
the start of a word is just its opening letter

blocks.note: first letter of the word
the Gents is a men's lavatory, where a urinal is found
a candidate who is elected is in

explanation.surface: A grumble that the men's toilets, left unelected, will bring the nation to ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gents is the British name for a men's public toilet; the surface makes it sound like a group of gentlemen standing for election.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural is the adjective for things belonging to the countryside rather than the town.

clue.text: Dramatic location, or senile resort?

indicators.note: read as re-sort, it asks for the letters to be sorted again into a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spa or seaside town where old people go, perhaps a spectacular setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday destination, which suits 'location', but it splits as re-sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Elsinore is the Danish castle where Shakespeare's Hamlet is set, a location in a famous drama.

clue.text: Wicked sex, enough to get by on

blocks.note: mean can describe someone nasty or cruel
S is an abbreviation for sex, as on forms

explanation.surface: Wild sex being all a person needs to survive.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a phrase describing a noun, enough money to live on.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's means are their income or resources, the money they have available to support themselves.

clue.text: Fancy assessing flatulence?

indicators.note: as a verb in the imperative, fancy means imagine anew, inviting a reworked arrangement of the letters

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A mock-surprised suggestion that someone would like to rate how much wind a person is breaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' reads like 'would you like to', but it signals the rearrangement of the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: Flatulence is having wind in the gut, which is exactly the condition of being gassy.

clue.text: It would calculate USA's ruin, being infiltrated by born again Christian leaders

indicators.note: a ruin is something wrecked and broken apart, so the letters are knocked out of order
leaders are those at the front, here the first letters of the words
something infiltrated has others slip inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: taken as written
first letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A prediction that America will be wrecked by evangelical Christians taking over.
explanation.walkthrough: The three letters of the country are rearranged and the initials of the religious phrase are slipped between the first and second of them.
explanation.definitionFit: An abacus is a frame of beads on wires used to do arithmetic, a device for calculating.

clue.text: But not if topless, without a tabloid

indicators.note: something topless has lost its top, so the opening letter comes off

blocks.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
less can mean minus or without

explanation.surface: A grumpy remark about a tabloid without its famous topless models.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid once known for topless photos on page three; 'topless' here strips the first letter from SUNLESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Unless means except if, so 'I will go unless it rains' is 'I will go, but not if it rains'.

clue.text: Deflated by peer, Blair abandons broadcast – "Snake!"

indicators.note: to abandon something is to leave it behind, so those letters are dropped

blocks.note: Tony Blair, former Labour prime minister
to air a programme is to broadcast it
the adder is Britain's venomous snake

explanation.surface: Tony Blair, put down by a member of the House of Lords, quits the airwaves and is denounced as a snake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peer' looks like a lord, but it is one who pees, and 'Deflated' is literal emptying.
explanation.definitionFit: The bladder is the organ that holds urine and goes slack when someone urinates, a punning use of peer as 'one who pees'.

clue.text: Corsets worn? Royal heir pissed off that Brenda does so?

definitions.text: Royal heir pissed off that Brenda does so?

blocks.note: stays are an old word for a corset
clothes being worn are on

explanation.surface: Royal underwear gossip: is Prince Charles annoyed that the Queen keeps her corsets on?
explanation.walkthrough: Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen; the definition jokes that Charles is fed up she keeps reigning.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay on is to remain in a post, which the Queen did for decades while her heir waited.

clue.text: Rich Saunders?

blocks.note: first meaning: laughable, as in 'that's rich'
second meaning: a comedian, such as Jennifer Saunders

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a wealthy person named Saunders; Jennifer Saunders is the British comedian of Absolutely Fabulous.
explanation.definitionFit: Comic works as an adjective for something ridiculous or laughable and as a noun for a comedian, of whom Saunders is an example.

clue.text: Hardly what the Tories got in June, so a massive descent

definitions.text: Hardly what the Tories got in June

blocks.clueFragment: Hardly what the Tories got in June
blocks.note: first meaning: an overwhelming election victory, which the 2017 election was not
second meaning: a huge fall of earth and rock down a slope

explanation.surface: A sneer at the Conservatives' poor June election result being a great fall.
explanation.walkthrough: Theresa May called a snap election in June 2017 expecting a huge majority and lost it; 'Hardly' marks the irony.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a crushing electoral win and a geological collapse of a hillside.

clue.text: Funny thing, to be an MP and almost put in an appearance

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is missing

blocks.note: MPs sit in Parliament, representing a seat
to come is to turn up

explanation.surface: The joke of being an MP who barely bothers to show up in Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: An MP is said to sit for a constituency.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitcom, short for situation comedy, is a television show meant to make people laugh.

clue.text: Number one spinner, fruity thing

blocks.note: a spinning top is a toy that spins
a banana is a fruit

explanation.surface: Praise for the best spin bowler as a bit of an odd character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinner' suggests a spin bowler in cricket, but it is the child's toy.
explanation.definitionFit: Top banana is slang for the leading person, the boss, the one in first place.

clue.text: Pervy rep, touching wives inappropriately, whiffs

indicators.note: pervy means perverted, and something perverted is twisted out of its proper form
done inappropriately means done improperly, so the letters fall into a wrong order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A seedy salesman who gropes married women and smells bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touching' just puts the two words side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A whiff can mean a faint hint or foretaste of something, so whiffs are advance glimpses, as previews are.

clue.text: Mike Pence partly avers "diversification"? Other way round

indicators.note: partly points to only one portion of the title being used, its first word
to diversify is to make varied and different, so the letters are turned into another form

blocks.note: Mike Pence was Vice President of the USA
taken as written

explanation.surface: The US Vice President half-heartedly backs diversity, or perhaps the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: Pence was Trump's Vice President, so part of his title supplies the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Vice versa is the Latin phrase meaning with the order or relation reversed.

clue.text: Electronic survey about POTUS: "No politician; civilization no longer"

indicators.note: saying no to something removes it, here the abbreviation for a member of parliament
to be about something is to surround it, so one piece is placed around another

blocks.note: E is the standard abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail
POTUS is President of the United States, then Donald Trump
to scan is to survey or look over

explanation.surface: An online poll about the President finds he is no politician and civilization is over.
explanation.walkthrough: MP is cut from the President's name, and E-SCAN goes around what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: The Etruscans were an ancient people of central Italy whose civilization was absorbed by Rome and vanished.

clue.text: Couple, taking Trump's lead, discharged with a bang

indicators.note: the lead is the one out in front, so only the opening letter is kept
something discharged is fired off or released, scattering the letters

blocks.note: taken as written
first letter of the name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pair, following Trump's example, were fired with a loud noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with a bang' reads as one phrase; it splits to give A plus the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bang is vulgar slang for having sex, and copulate is the formal verb for the same act.

clue.text: Member's position: "Corbyn's 'lead' bollocks – check"

indicators.note: the lead is the one at the front, so only the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: first letter of the name
bollocks is British slang for nonsense, as is rot
CH is the chess abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: An MP's stance on Jeremy Corbyn's leadership: that it is nonsense and needs reining in.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeremy Corbyn was then the Labour leader; 'bollocks' is British slang for testicles and also for rubbish talk.
explanation.definitionFit: The member here is the penis, and its position is the crotch, where the legs join the body.

clue.text: One caught short with drink is a 29

blocks.note: a means one
ct is the short form of caught on a cricket scorecard
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Someone suddenly needing the toilet after drinking is a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught short' is British for urgently needing a toilet; here it means the shortened form of caught.
explanation.definitionFit: To act up is to misbehave, which is what someone who is a pain in the arse (29) does.

clue.text: Idler's shit, full of rubbish

indicators.note: something full of another thing holds it inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: poo is a childish word for excrement
tat is cheap worthless stuff

explanation.surface: A lazy person's droppings are full of junk.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A couch potato is a lazy person who lounges in front of the television, so the vegetable stands for an idler.

clue.text: Working with a Conservative aristocrat, getting interim payment

definitions.note: a noun phrase for an adverbial phrase: paid on account

blocks.note: a machine that is on is working
taken as written
C is the abbreviation for Conservative
a count is a European nobleman

explanation.surface: Teaming up with a Tory noble to get an advance on your fee.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a noun phrase while the answer is adverbial: a sum paid on account is an interim payment.
explanation.definitionFit: Money paid on account is a partial sum handed over in advance of the full settlement.

clue.text: Conservative leader blowing top – interrupt!

indicators.note: blowing off the top removes what is uppermost, the first letter

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
Vladimir Putin, the Russian leader

explanation.surface: A Tory leader losing their temper and telling someone to butt in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blowing top' suggests a fit of anger, but here it lops the first letter off a world leader.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut in is to break into a conversation while someone else is speaking.

clue.text: A hard man ought to get screwed

indicators.note: something screwed is twisted round, so the letters are turned into another order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A crude remark that a macho man deserves sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'screwed' carries a sexual sense in the surface but works as a twisting signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough is a noun for a violent, rough man, a thug or heavy.

clue.text: Bring up Vaz's source? Give it a miss!

indicators.note: a source is where something starts, so only the opening letter is used

blocks.note: first letter of the name
to omit something is to leave it out

explanation.surface: Advice not to raise the matter of where Keith Vaz got his information.
explanation.walkthrough: Keith Vaz was a Labour MP caught in a 2016 scandal; 'Bring up' suggests raising a topic.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring up food is to be sick, an everyday idiom for the same thing.

clue.text: What might you be holding against Private Eye, wise guy?

blocks.note: the reader is holding a magazine as they solve
the magazine speaking of itself is us

explanation.surface: A smart-aleck asking what grudge the reader bears against Private Eye.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is printed in Private Eye, so the setter calls the reader's copy a mag and the magazine itself us; 'holding against' suggests a grudge.
explanation.definitionFit: A magus is a wise man or sage, as with the Magi who visited the infant Jesus.

clue.text: Two Conservatives taking strange oath, one like the state of the government?

definitions.text: like the state of the government

indicators.note: strange means odd and out of the ordinary, so the letters take an unusual order
to take something is to hold it within, so one piece is placed inside others

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative, twice
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A pair of Tories swearing an odd oath, one of them as messy as the cabinet.
explanation.walkthrough: The two Cs sit either side of the rearranged five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaotic means in complete disorder, the setter's satirical view of how the government was functioning.

clue.text: Out of control Trump (sigh, no leader!) dumping millions for good

indicators.note: with no leader, the word has lost its front letter
to dump something is to get rid of it, so those letters are thrown out
something out of control runs wild, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written
M is the abbreviation for million
the word with its first letter removed

explanation.surface: A despairing sigh at a wild, leaderless Trump shedding millions for a worthy cause.
explanation.walkthrough: M is removed from TRUMP and S from SIGH; the remaining seven letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Upright describes someone honest and moral, which is one sense of good.

clue.text: Dodgy hen parties including one in drag

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or dubious, suggesting letters that are not in their proper order

blocks.note: taken as written
a means one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Rowdy bachelorette parties that feature a man dressed as a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Hen parties are British pre-wedding nights out for the bride and her friends; 'in drag' wants to mean cross-dressed, but 'in' is fodder and 'drag' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A drag is something tedious or irritating, and a pain in the arse is the vulgar British idiom for the same.
